item.title: Madang Government urged to support koniak farmers
item.description: Bilake Enape Waizepa hands over the vehicle’s key to Justin and his wife (NBC News) The Madang Provincial Government has been urged to support koniak farmers in the province, especially in terms of creating road access for them to bring their produce to the markets in town.
item.content:encoded:
Bilake Enape Waizepa hands over the vehicle’s key to Justin and his wife (NBC News)

The Madang Provincial Government has been urged to support koniak farmers in the province, especially in terms of creating road access for them to bring their produce to the markets in town.

The call was made by the Managing Director of Ocean Kava Limited, a local buyer and exporter of Koniak, Madang's very own Kava.

Bilake Enape Waizepa extended the farmers' call recently whilst presenting a new Isuzu dyna vehicle to a local farmer.

Mr Waizepa said many of the Koniak farmers come from remote villages that have no road links and transport remains their biggest challenge when trying to bring their produce into town.

"Koniak farmers come from very remote locations, unlike cocoa and copra farmers; most of whom have easy access to road transport. Some of our farmers carry their koniak and walk for 2 to 3 days before getting on a PMV or boat to come to town just to sell their produce.

"Koniak is now transforming the livelihoods of rural families in Madang. It is directly putting K3 million to K4 million into farmers' pockets annually.

"They, however; need a little push from the government, especially with transport assistance. For those farmers in Raikos and on Karkar Island, they need bigger boats to move their koniak bags to Madang town. The small boats are not safe during times of strong winds and high seas," Mr Waizepa said.

He added that Koniak farmers in Madang Province have not received any form of assistance from the government since they started some six to seven years ago.

Despite their struggles, Mr Waizepa continues to encourage them to work hard.

The company has created a partnership program with the farmers to help them purchase materials like roofing sheets, iron posts, farming tools and/ or vehicles, boats, and other necessities to improve their livelihoods in the village.

Last week, it gave away another truck to a farmer under the partnership program.

The company's owner and Managing Director, Bilake Enape Waizepa, handed over a brand new Isuzu dyna to farmer Justin and his wife under the partnership program.

Justin from Simbai grows Koniak in his wife's village, Basken on Madang's north coast, and has been selling to Ocean Kava for two years.

However, his farm income over the last two years has been kept by the company under the program until it accumulated to over a hundred and thirty thousand kina, enough to purchase an Isuzu dyna.

Justin and his wife drove away a happy and satisfied couple last Tuesday with their first vehicle.

They were the fourth vehicle recipients.

The first three farmers got a Toyota Landcruiser, an Isuzu Dyna, and an open back utility.

Mr Bilake told farmers who witnessed Justin receive his Isuzu dyna from the company last week that nothing is impossible if they commit themselves to what they do are doing.

He said, "Justin's story should serve as an inspiration to other farmers to continue to work hard."

Ocean Kava Limited is one of Madang's leading buyers and exporters with secured markets in Fiji, Australia, New Zealand, China, and other countries.

It currently exports up to 100 tonnes annually.

Waizepa, meanwhile; plans to build a koniak processing facility in the nation's capital in order to add value to the product and to help create employment for the young people.

He added,"Nothing is impossible if you trust yourself and put your heart whole heart into what you're doing."

Justin said that as a simple carpenter, he did not think he would be successful one day.

He thanked Ocean Kava for introducing the partnership program to farmers, a lot of whom are already benefiting from it.

item.title: Biggest lesson in Uni is not about GPA; ‘Attitude’
item.description: Members of the UPNG Kerowagi Students Association and police after launching their Educational Awareness in Kerowagi District. The team will visit all high and secondary schools in the district (Supplied) When Peter William left Kerowagi district in Simbu for the University of Papua New Guinea, he went with a lot of questions and very little guidance.
item.content:encoded:
Members of the UPNG Kerowagi Students Association and police after launching their Educational Awareness in Kerowagi District. The team will visit all high and secondary schools in the district (Supplied)

When Peter William left Kerowagi district in Simbu for the University of Papua New Guinea, he went with a lot of questions and very little guidance.

This week, he came back, not alone to make sure the next lot of Kerowagi kids don't have to struggle like he did.

No one had told him what GPA he needed. No one had explained which subjects matched which course. He had to learn it all on his own.

Peter, now President of the UPNG Kerowagi Students Association, led a team of UPNG students back to Kerowagi District to launch an Educational Awareness Program for high school students.

Their first stops yesterday were Moroma Adventist High School and Kunabau EBC High School.

And the message was simple: 'You can do it too, but you need to start now'.

"We want our younger brothers and sisters in Kerowagi to know what is required to enter UPNG. We shared the entry GPAs, the subject combinations for each course, and the new programs that have been introduced at UPNG" Peter said.

Instead of just handing out pamphlets, the team stood in front of the students, one student for each of UPNG's five schools and talked to them like big brothers and sisters.

They talked about what subjects to pick, what grades to aim for, and what university life is really like.

But Peter said the biggest lesson was not about GPA. It was about attitude.

"We encouraged them to believe in themselves, to put God first in everything they do, to set their priorities right, and to work hard towards achieving their goals. We reminded them to read a lot of books and to write as much as they can, because knowledge truly is power."

For many of the high school students listening, it was the first time someone from their own district, who sits in the same classrooms they dream about, had come back to explain it to them in their own language.

The team was welcomed warmly by school administrations, teachers and communities.

The program was supported by Simbu Provincial Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Mazuc Rubiang and Senior Sergeant Julie Gale, who assisted with security and transport on Day One.

Peter thanked the sponsors, the two schools, teachers, communities and all who made the first day possible.

The team will now visit the remaining high and secondary schools across Kerowagi District in the coming days.

He said It is a small idea with a big heart: If you have made it out, go back and pull the next one up.

"Put God first. Dream big. Work hard. Stay focused." Said Peter William

item.title: Modilon General Hospital receives life-saving medical equipment
item.description: PNG Chamber of Resources & Energy Executive Director Richard Kassman (third from left) addressing the Modilon Hospital staff in Madang during the delivery of the pediatric lifesaving medical equipment on Monday (Supplied) Children and infants across Madang province will receive improved life-saving medical care following the official handover of critical paediatric and neonatal equipment to Modilo
item.content:encoded:
PNG Chamber of Resources & Energy Executive Director Richard Kassman (third from left) addressing the Modilon Hospital staff in Madang during the delivery of the pediatric lifesaving medical equipment on Monday (Supplied)

Children and infants across Madang province will receive improved life-saving medical care following the official handover of critical paediatric and neonatal equipment to Modilon General Hospital on Monday.

Funded through the PNG Chamber of Resources & Energy (PNGCORE) Charity Golf Challenge Program. More than K300, 000 was used from the 2025 Charity Golf Challenge to purchase the equipment.

Specialised respiratory, neonatal, and paediatric equipment was purchased to strengthen emergency response and improve treatment outcomes for critically ill young patients.

Speaking at the handover, PNGCORE Executive Director Richard Kassman OBE paid tribute to the hospital's medical workforce, emphasising that medical tools are only as effective as the people who use them.

"While we are pleased to help provide these medical tools, the real heroes are the doctors, nurses, and health workers at Modilon General Hospital who show up every day with unwavering dedication to save lives.

"Their commitment to caring for Madang's children under challenging circumstances is truly inspiring. Our role is simply to stand behind them and ensure they have the resources they need to do what they do best."Mr Kassman said.

Kassman said, a vibrant and thriving industry is what makes initiatives like this possible.

“When our resources and energy sector is strong and growing, it generates the economic momentum and capacity for businesses to contribute more to the national economy.”

Kassman thanked the corporate sponsors and community partners whose support made the donation possible.

The Charity Golf Challenge's expansion was made possible through 33 organisations across the resources, energy, professional services, financial services, insurance, and community sectors, including major contributors K92 Mining Limited, Sun Engineering, and McMonagle Qld and Santos Limited.

Modilon Hospital Chief Executive Officer Dr Martin Daimen welcomed the new diagnostic and respiratory tools, noting that the equipment will immediately strengthen the clinical team's emergency response, neonatal resuscitation, and daily care across the province.

“On behalf of our doctors, nurses, clinical teams, and the families we serve, I extend our sincere gratitude to every organisation that contributed to this initiative.

"These resources will directly support our staff as they respond to medical emergencies, perform neonatal resuscitation, and manage respiratory distress for our most vulnerable patients.” Dr Daimen said.

The impact of this support will be felt by families across Madang Province for years to come.

First batch of equipment includes advanced respiratory support systems, such as Fisher & Paykel Bubble CPAP machines and Airvo 3 Humidified High Flow devices for infants in respiratory distress, alongside nebulisers, clinical thermometers, nursing stethoscopes, manual and digital paediatric blood pressure cuffs, and other diagnostic tools.

Remaining items will arrive in the coming weeks.

This contribution marks the second major provincial healthcare project delivered through the Charity Golf Challenge. Following the Port Moresby tournament on 17 July 2026, the next Charity Golf Challenge is scheduled for 27 November 2026 during PNG Investment Week in Sydney, Australia, with funds being set aside to support a third provincial hospital in 2027.

item.title: PA responds to Boram airport land compensation concerns
item.description: Acting East Sepik Provincial Administrator, Samson Torovi (NBC News) The East Sepik Provincial Administration has clarified its position on the K9.2 million State ex-gratia payment for local landowners affected by the Boram Airport Redevelopment Project, following concerns raised by representatives of the Moem, Koikin and Makun communities.
item.content:encoded:
Acting East Sepik Provincial Administrator, Samson Torovi (NBC News)

The East Sepik Provincial Administration has clarified its position on the K9.2 million State ex-gratia payment for local landowners affected by the Boram Airport Redevelopment Project, following concerns raised by representatives of the Moem, Koikin and Makun communities.

According to a media statement issued by the Office of the Provincial Administrator, the State, through the Department of Lands and Physical Planning, had agreed to pay K9.2 million to local landowners for giving up their interests in the land required for the project.

The statement also confirmed that an initial K5 million was transferred into the East Sepik Provincial Government's Operating Account on September 29, 2026.

However, the release of the compensation remains subject to the identification of the rightful landowners.

Acting Provincial Administrator Samson Torovi said the administration must first establish which groups are the legitimate owners of the land before any payment is considered.

He explained that representatives of the Moem, Koikin and Makun communities had raised concerns at the Provincial Administration Headquarters at BMS Kreer Heights, demanding the release of the funds while questioning the entitlement of certain landowner groups.

In response, Mr Torovi said he had directed the Provincial Management Team, through the Provincial Lands Advisor and Legal Advisor, to meet with the groups and look into their different land ownership claims.

He said the process would help identify the rightful landowners and their respective clans before the compensation was released.

Mr Torovi assured the communities that the administration was not withholding legitimate landowner entitlements. He said the aim was to ensure that the money reached the rightful beneficiaries through a fair and transparent process.

He also called on all landowner groups and community leaders to remain patient while the verification process takes place.

Meanwhile, the Boram Airport Redevelopment Project is being carried out under the National Airports Corporation's Civil Aviation Development Investment Program II. The project includes the construction of a new airport terminal and runway extension.

Mr Torovi said the project was important for East Sepik Province and urged all parties to work together to resolve the outstanding concerns without unnecessary confrontation or disruption to the project.

item.title: Basil calls for highway repairs
item.description: Bulolo MP Sam Basil Jr is calling on the National Government to urgently fix the Lae–Bulolo Highway, saying its poor condition continues to affect passengers, businesses and communities. The highway connects Lae, Bulolo and Wau and is used daily by people travelling between the towns and villages.
item.content:encoded:
Bulolo MP Sam Basil Jr is calling on the National Government to urgently fix the Lae–Bulolo Highway, saying its poor condition continues to affect passengers, businesses and communities.

The highway connects Lae, Bulolo and Wau and is used daily by people travelling between the towns and villages.

However, many sections of the road are in poor condition, with potholes, loose gravel and dust making travel difficult for motorists and passengers.

During the rainy season, travelling becomes even harder, especially at Kumalu Creek, where flooding can stop vehicles and trucks from crossing.

Passengers travelling along the highway face long delays, uncomfortable journeys and difficulties reaching their destinations on time.

Basil Jr says he has raised concerns about the highway many times because of its importance to Bulolo District and the wider Morobe economy.

The road is also used by businesses in agriculture, mining and forestry to transport workers, supplies and products.

Companies such as Zenag, PNG Forest Products and Hidden Valley Mine depend on the highway for their daily operations.

Basil says the National Government and the responsible authorities must give the road urgent attention.

He says fixing the highway will make travel easier and safer for passengers, help businesses move their goods and improve access for communities along the road.

He is also calling for attention to be given to Kumalu Creek, where flooding continues to cause problems for road users during heavy rain.

item.title: MBPHA health workers stage peaceful protest
item.description: (Front) Gloria Warren, MBPHA Board Chairperson, standing beside her MBPHA CEO Dr Perista Mamadi listening during the peaceful protest (NBC News) ‎Medical staff, including clinicians and non-clinicians at the Alotau Provincial Hospital held a peaceful administrative protest yesterday morning at the front of the Milne Bay Health Authority (MBPHA) Administration office, demanding urgent intervention
item.content:encoded:
(Front) Gloria Warren, MBPHA Board Chairperson, standing beside her MBPHA CEO Dr Perista Mamadi listening during the peaceful protest (NBC News)

‎Medical staff, including clinicians and non-clinicians at the Alotau Provincial Hospital held a peaceful administrative protest yesterday morning at the front of the Milne Bay Health Authority (MBPHA) Administration office, demanding urgent intervention into the human resource management and the recruitment failures which has caused increased workload on existing staffs

‎‎A 48- hour ultimatum has been given by the petitioners for hospital management and board to respond to their demands.

‎Medical practitioners, clinical support staff, allied health staff, nurses, community health workers and non-clinical staff assembled outside MBPHA Administration office yesterday and presented a formal petition to the hospital's senior executive management and board of directors.

‎The petition raises serious concerns over human resource management, especially the alleged incompetence in staff recruitment, chronic delays and procedural inefficiencies leaving critical positions vacant.

‎The petition also highlights Leadership accountability, the lack of responsiveness to clinical workforce needs, Human Resource department operations, declining management credibility and the departure of consultants and senior clinicians.

‎‎The petitioners warn that continued failure to recruit essential personnel poses a serious risk to service delivery, patient outcomes and the overall health and wellbeing of the population served by the hospital.

‎Representing the medical team, Physician Dr Dennis Tony presented two binded- booklets containing their petition to the Senior Executive Management and the hospital Board of Directors to immediately look into their demands.

‎Dr Tony said their intention is not to criticize anyone but to formally communicate issues affecting the staff and their wellbeing.

‎"The intention is not to criticize anyone but rather to ensure concerns affecting staff and the quality service, as well the institution is formally communicated through appropriate governing body".

‎"It is our hope that the petition will serve as a beginning of a positive and constructive process and are confident that through open communication and mutual respect and a shared commitment to the organization’s mission, solutions can be found that will benefit the staff and the management and people the hospital serves.” Dr Tony said.

‎In receiving the petition, MBPHA Board Chairperson, Mrs Gloria Warren, said in her five years as Chairperson, no discussion was made known as to issues surrounding the hospital and will gladly look into this and come up with a favorable response.

‎"Within my five years as chair, this is the first petition presented. I as a chair, I've heard so much. We've been having board meetings; we never receive anything as to the issues affecting the sectors in the hospital. We will now sit and discuss and come up with a good resolution". Warren said.

‎The petitioners have demanded that the board respond within 48- hours on submission. Failure to respond within the stipulated timeframe, the matter will then be further escalated to Provincial Government and Department of Health, relevant oversight and accountability bodies and public disclosure through professional associations and stakeholder forums.

item.title: Nasfund opens new office in Wewak
item.description: National Superannuation Fund (Nasfund) members in East Sepik Province will now have access to improved customer services following the official opening of its new modern branch office on the third floor of Tangmow Plaza in Wewak Town. The new service centre can accommodate up to 20 members at a time and features four dedicated customer service counters to assist members with their enquiries and su
item.content:encoded:
National Superannuation Fund (Nasfund) members in East Sepik Province will now have access to improved customer services following the official opening of its new modern branch office on the third floor of Tangmow Plaza in Wewak Town.

The new service centre can accommodate up to 20 members at a time and features four dedicated customer service counters to assist members with their enquiries and superannuation needs.

Speaking during the official opening ceremony yeasterday, Nasfund Board Director representing the Employees Federation and Chairwoman of the Nasfund Membership Committee, Florence Willy, said despite losing its previous branch office in a fire, Nasfund remained committed to maintaining its operations in Wewak.

“We lost our previous branch through fire; our service did not stop. We actually continued our operations here in Wewak,” Ms Willy said.

She further highlighted that Nasfund currently serves more than 24,000 members in East Sepik, reaffirming the fund's commitment to continuing its services to members in the province.

Meanwhile, speaking on behalf of Nasfund Chief Executive Officer, Alex Rogea, the General Manager for Talent and Culture reaffirmed the institution's commitment to serving the people of Papua New Guinea.

“We have a higher responsibility, a noble responsibility of safeguarding the retirement savings of our people here in PNG and also here in East Sepik,” Rogea said.

The new branch office was blessed by Bishop Jozef Roszynski SVD of the Wewak Catholic Diocese in the presence of invited stakeholders and guests.

item.title: TISA opens 8th bank in Mt Hagen
item.description: Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa (right) cutting the ribbon marking the officially operation of TISA Bank in Mt Hagen yesterday November 09th (NBC News) TISA Bank has expanded its banking services into Western Highlands Province, officially opening its 8th branch in Mt Hagen yesterday, November 9, together with its first Automated Teller Machine (ATM) outside of Port Moresby.
item.content:encoded:
Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa (right) cutting the ribbon marking the officially operation of TISA Bank in Mt Hagen yesterday November 09th (NBC News)

TISA Bank has expanded its banking services into Western Highlands Province, officially opening its 8th branch in Mt Hagen yesterday, November 9, together with its first Automated Teller Machine (ATM) outside of Port Moresby.

The new branch, located at Wamp Nga Haus is expected to provide greater access to banking services for individuals, teachers, small businesses and communities across the province and the Highlands region.

Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa, who officially opened the branch, acknowledged TISA’s long contribution to the province and the Highlands region, dating back to its beginnings as a savings and loan society.

Governor Rapa also welcomed TISA’s decision to invest in Mt Hagen, saying the move shows growing confidence in the province’s business environment.

"More businesses are beginning to invest in Western Highlands, and the provincial government will continue working to provide a secure and supportive environment for businesses and financial institutions," stressed Governor Rapa.

Rapa says the provincial government will continue to work alongside TISA and other financial institutions to strengthen economic activities in the province.

TISA Head of Retail Noel Keyala says the bank’s expansion is part of its mission to improve financial inclusion by reaching people who remain underbanked or have no access to formal banking services.

"TISA’s investment in banking services is not simply about new technology, but about making banking more convenient and accessible to Papua New Guineans."

"The bank’s success should be measured not only by the infrastructure it builds, but also by the opportunities it creates the communities it supports and the lasting impact it has on people’s lives," outlines the Head of TISA Retail Mr Keyala.

The Mt Hagen branch will provide full banking services, including deposits and withdrawals, new account openings, Visa debit cards, loans and general banking assistance.

The branch will particularly serve educators, small-to-medium enterprises and everyday customers in Western Highlands and the Highlands region with its customer base of more than 5,000 in the region.

TISA began in 1972 as the Teachers Savings and Loan Society (TSL), established to provide savings and loan services to educators in Papua New Guinea.

Over more than five decades, it grew into the country’s largest savings and loan society and the Pacific’s largest credit union, before transitioning into commercial banking.

TISA was officially granted a commercial banking license by the Bank of Papua New Guinea on October 8, 2024, and became TISA Bank Limited.

Governor Rapa cut the ribbon to the new branch and unveiled the ATM, formally marking the start of TISA’s commercial banking operations in Mt Hagen.
